query_analysis.original_query: Calculate the theoretical minimum energy required to separate a binary gas-liquid mixture under isothermal conditions. The feed stream contains 60 mol% Component A and 40 mol% Component B, entering at a pressure of 5 bar and a temperature of 298 K. The desired products are a gas stream with 95 mol% Component A and a liquid stream with 90 mol% Component B. Assume ideal gas and liquid behavior, and neglect heat losses or inefficiencies in the separation process.
query_analysis.expanded_query: Using thermodynamic principles and ideal behavior assumptions, calculate the minimum theoretical energy required to separate a binary gas-liquid mixture under isothermal conditions. The feed stream contains 60 mol% Component A and 40 mol% Component B at 5 bar and 298 K, and the desired products are a gas stream with 95 mol% Component A and a liquid stream with 90 mol% Component B. Neglect heat losses or inefficiencies in the separation process.

selected_agents.role: Perform thermodynamic analysis to calculate minimum energy required

communication_strategy.information_flow: Thermodynamic parameters defined and calculations performed
communication_strategy.collaboration_protocol: Iterative collaboration to validate thermodynamic formulas and mathematical results

clarification_questions: Should we consider any pressure changes during the separation, or assume a constant pressure of 5 bar throughout?
Are there any specific properties of Components A and B that need to be considered beyond ideal behavior?
